title: How Much Can Gaussian Dependence Inflate the Benjamini-Hochberg Procedure's FDR?
summary: We study the worst-case false discovery rate (FDR) of the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure for both one- and two-sided Gaussian tests with general correlation matrices. For each setting and given target FDR level $q$, we construct a family of finite Gaussian models whose FDR divided by $q$ diverges as $q\downarrow0$. This disproves any universal multiplicative FDR bound. Moreover, we establish new FDR lower bounds that are independent of the number of hypotheses.
